clue.text: Josephine having task linked to a desert plant

parts.note: Jo is a short form of the name Josephine
a job is a task

explanation.surface: Josephine has a chore connected with some cactus in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Jojoba is a shrub native to the deserts of the American south-west, grown for its oil.

clue.text: In France, I will get on top of a really nasty bad emotion

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece getting on top of the rest means it is placed before them

parts.note: je is the French word for I
lousy means really nasty or very bad

explanation.surface: A French speaker announces they will overcome something truly unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy or possessive resentment is a classic negative feeling, one of the deadly sins in spirit.

clue.text: Sort of open, but not offering a first drink

indicators.note: not offering the opening A means the word gives up its leading letter A

parts.note: a door that is ajar is slightly, or sort of, open

explanation.surface: Someone half-opens a door but is stingy about the first round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not offering' takes A, the first letter, off AJAR. In Britain 'a jar' is informal for a drink at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is British slang for a drink, especially a glass of beer, as in going for a jar.

clue.text: Crew heading for boat, appearing disorderly

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ragged means untidy or disorderly

explanation.surface: A boat's crew sets off looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like a noun for a boat's team, but it is the past tense of the verb crow, meaning boasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew is the past tense of crow, to boast, which is the same as boasted.

clue.text: Cry of surprise that's repeated precisely by an islander

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
sic is written after a quoted word to show it is reproduced exactly as it was

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in astonishment, and an islander echoes it word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'; SIC, Latin for 'thus', marks a quotation copied exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Corsica, the French Mediterranean island, is a person from an island.

clue.text: Former students to attempt radio-based series of lectures —— it's not easy to complete

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: old boys (OBS) are former students, and to tackle is to attempt
a course is a series of lectures or classes

explanation.surface: Alumni try out a broadcast lecture series that proves very hard to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: OBS is short for old boys, former pupils of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: A course full of hurdles, walls and nets is hard work to get round, by design.

clue.text: Awkward character who's apparently mediocre?

definitions.meaning: a tiresome or unpleasant person, a euphemism for something ruder
mediocre is so-so, and the phrase looks like '...' joined, as if so-so

explanation.surface: Describing a difficult person who seems merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite stand-in for an insult aimed at an annoying person, and split it looks like so-so.

clue.text: Money-making scheme suggested by character on links?

indicators.note: on here means attached to or following, so the character comes after the links

parts.note: a chain is a series of links
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A get-rich-quick plan hinted at by a golfer on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests a golf course, but it means the links of a chain; 'on' attaches the character after the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter promises rewards to recipients who send copies or money on, a pyramid-style scheme.

clue.text: Old French name associated with Italian opera

parts.note: Norma is an opera by the Italian composer Bellini

explanation.surface: A French name of long ago linked to a work at La Scala.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman French was the dialect of Old French spoken by the Normans who conquered England.

clue.text: Light accompaniment to food, nothing very substantial

parts.note: a window lets light in, so it can be called a light
a dressing goes with food, as on a salad

explanation.surface: A light salad dressing is hardly a filling meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Window dressing means a superficial show put on to impress, with little real substance behind it.

clue.text: Arcade? It is a disfigurement in Greek resort area

indicators.note: a disfigurement mangles the shape of the letters, and Greek suggests something unintelligible, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An amusement arcade is called a blot on a Greek holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disfigurement in Greek' rearranges ARCADEITISA; 'Greek' tempts as part of the definition, but this sea lies between Italy and the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic coast is lined with holiday beaches, so the sea serves as a resort region.

clue.text: Duo not needing piano for song

indicators.note: not needing a thing means doing without it, so it is removed

parts.note: a pair is a duo
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A singing pair manage without accompaniment for their number.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, so a song.

clue.text: Old book told tales about head of games, as required

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: lied means told untruths, told tales

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ancient volume spun yarns about the chief of the games, as demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obliged to do something is to be required or compelled to do it.

clue.text: One behaving unstably in the firing line?

definitions.text: One behaving unstably in the firing line?

parts.words: One behaving unstably in the firing line?
parts.note: pictures a gun on a ship broken free of its mountings, then an unpredictable person liable to cause damage

explanation.surface: An erratic soldier among those in the line of fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpredictable person who causes trouble is likened to a gun rolling free on a ship's deck.

clue.text: A divine conclusion before a collection of extra material

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine, a cleric
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: A clergyman's final remarks come before an appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a clergyman or theologian; DD is the degree Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added to a book or document, extra material appended to the main text.

clue.text: Circus performer in potentially cut-throat business?

definitions.text: Circus performer in potentially cut-throat business?

parts.words: Circus performer in potentially cut-throat business?
parts.note: an entertainer whose act sends a blade down the throat, a job that could literally cut it

explanation.surface: A big-top act working in a ruthless trade.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer pushes a blade down the gullet, so a slip could literally cut the throat.

clue.text: Lottery's first huge win possibly leads to booze

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way
the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A big lottery prize may lead to heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Glühwein is German mulled wine, a warm alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Guess London, say, as source of investment

parts.note: to venture a guess is to hazard one, so venture means guess
London is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: Speculating about the city as a place to raise funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new businesses, a source of funding for start-ups.

clue.text: Pirates' at sea make slow progress

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Buccaneers out on the ocean plod slowly along.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, trudging along slowly.

clue.text: Exercise getting newspapers in revolt

parts.note: newspapers collectively are the press
up means in revolt, as in up in arms

explanation.surface: Journalists are rising up in revolt during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, called a push-up in America, is a floor exercise lifting the body with the arms.

clue.text: Double reserve almost, holding up number of images

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses another
double means the piece is written twice
almost means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: ice is coolness of manner, reserve

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: A pair of reservists nearly support a number of pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ICE to IC, and 'Double' makes ICIC; 'up' turns NO into ON, which 'holding' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Iconic, from icon, literally means relating to images or likenesses.

clue.text: Endlessly stupid about tax for neckwear

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds another
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Someone foolish forever goes on about the tax on ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts CRASS to CRAS; VAT is Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Cravats are scarves or wide ties worn around the neck, items of neckwear.

clue.text: Track down her aunt abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Locating one's aunt who lives overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to discover or find out, as to track down something hidden.

clue.text: Sister's part of speech neglecting love

definitions.note: read as Sister is, the definition followed by a link

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving something out

parts.note: a noun is a part of speech
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A sister's share of conversation ignores romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister in a religious order is a member of a convent.

clue.text: Hideaway? Here's pistol, if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling on a hidden gun in a secret refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if disturbed' rearranges HERESPISTOL. The question mark marks the definition as an example: such a room was one kind of hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden chambers were built in English Catholic houses to conceal clergy during persecution, a kind of hiding place.

clue.text: Escaped defeat, dispatching runs

indicators.note: dispatching means sending something away, so it is removed

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer avoided losing despite giving away runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out is to be free or away, as an escaped prisoner is out.

clue.text: Come together to study the roadside

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over
a verge is the grass strip at the roadside

explanation.surface: Gathering to examine the edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to meet or move towards the same point.

clue.text: Lad captures trophy displaying great accuracy

indicators.note: captures means holds inside

parts.note: a son is a lad
a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A boy wins a cup with pinpoint skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on means exactly right, precise.
